mechanism_fit: HB (M19 sink blame; tags M19, M6, M2). The numeric time-zone rule of FastDatePrinter ('Z'/'ZZ') is refactored by context edits into public static helpers in four classes over two packages. H1 is FastDatePrinter.appendZoneOffset; it writes the sign and the whole hours of the magnitude, and takes the minute field from G. G is DateUtils.offsetMinuteField; its javadoc promises 0..59 'whatever the sign of the offset'. H3 is DateFormatUtils.appendHourMinute; it passes both fields on as given. S is CharUtils.appendTwoDigits; its javadoc states the precondition 'must already be in the range 0 to 99; it is placed as given ... with no range check', and its two lines (value / 10 + '0', value % 10 + '0') visibly lack any sign or range step. The fault is the quiet omission of Math.abs on G's one assignment line (a plain division of the signed offset). The trigger calls the public entry DateFormatUtils.format(long, String, TimeZone, Locale) for GMT+05:30 and GMT-03:30. The west zone comes out as -03:-0: the sink writes the tens digit -3 of G's -30 as '-', so the odd character appears at the sink.
gold: org.apache.commons.lang3.time.DateUtils::offsetMinuteField (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtils.java). Fault: `final int totalMinutes = Math.abs(offsetMillis) / (60 * 1000);` becomes `final int totalMinutes = offsetMillis / (60 * 1000);`. Minimal repair: restore Math.abs.
decoys: org.apache.commons.lang3.CharUtils::appendTwoDigits (S, sink; new helper; documents the 0..99 precondition, placed as given)
org.apache.commons.lang3.time.DateFormatUtils::appendHourMinute (H3; new helper; writes HH[:]MM through S, values passed on as given)
org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDatePrinter::appendZoneOffset (H1; new helper; sign, whole hours of the magnitude via inline negation, minute field = G(offsetMillis))
org.apache.commons.lang3.time.DateFormatUtils::format (E; unchanged upstream; decl 'final long millis, final String pattern, final TimeZone timeZone, final Locale locale')
ownership_reason: CharUtils.appendTwoDigits (the sink) documents its precondition: the value must already be in 0..99 and is placed as given, digit by digit, with no range check; it does exactly that. DateFormatUtils.appendHourMinute documents that it passes both fields on as given, and does. FastDatePrinter.appendZoneOffset documents the sign ('-' for a negative offset), the hour field (whole hours of the magnitude, which it gets by negating the truncated hours for a negative offset) and that the minute field is DateUtils.offsetMinuteField(offsetMillis); it passes the signed offset, which that helper's contract accepts ('may be negative'). DateUtils.offsetMinuteField documents the postcondition: the minutes left over after the whole hours of the offset's MAGNITUDE, always 0..59 whatever the sign (+05:30 and -05:30 both give 30). On the variant it divides the signed offset, so GMT-03:30 (-12600000 ms) gives -210 % 60 = -30, and the sink, as documented, writes the tens digit -3 as the character '-' (48-3=45), producing -03:-0. The east zone +05:30 in the same trigger is formatted correctly, and the existing FastDatePrinterTest.testFormat (America/New_York -0500/-04:00) still passes on the variant, so the sign and hour path of appendZoneOffset, appendHourMinute and the sink are exercised and correct; only whole-hour negative offsets were ever tested, which is why the omission is latent. Restoring Math.abs in offsetMinuteField alone makes the trigger and the full suite pass. The declared one-line edits at the decoys do not absorb it: negating the offset at the call site breaks +05:30, reducing modulo 60 in appendHourMinute keeps -30, and taking abs of the sink's units digit leaves the '-' tens digit.
trigger: org.apache.commons.lang3.time.DateFormatUtilsTest::testHalfHourZonesEitherSideOfUtc (new JUnit4 method). It formats the instant 1000000000000L with pattern "ZZ" and Locale.US in TimeZone GMT+05:30 and in GMT-03:30, both custom fixed-offset zones with no DST, so the result does not depend on tzdata. It asserts east + " " + west equals "+05:30 -03:30". The east zone is included so that negating the offset at the H1 call site does not absorb the fault.
construction_notes: Design 1. Validator attempt 1: overall READY (rejected by audit on leakage; see revision). Validator attempt 2, after the javadoc-example change: overall READY, with G0-G13 all passing (G6 saw the gold and all 4 decoys). Packaged as CTV-49DDB6. By hand in a /private/tmp scratch copy: the CORRECT config passed the full suite with 0 failures. The variant failed only the trigger, with the signature above. The three declared compensating edits were each checked: the trigger still fails. (1) H1 negates the offset passed to G, which breaks +05:30. (2) H3 takes minutes % 60, which keeps -30. (3) The sink takes abs of the units digit, which keeps the '-' tens digit. Why the omission is latent: the existing suite formats Z/ZZ only for whole-hour zones (America/New_York, GMT-3, GMT-8, GMT+1, GMT+5, Reykjavik, MST7MDT ...). For those, G's minute field is 0 with or without abs, while the hours, sign and sink are exercised (FastDatePrinterTest.testFormat expects -0500/-05:00). Context edits are behaviour-preserving: for |offset| >= 0, (|offset|/60000) % 60 == |offset|/60000 - 60*(|offset|/3600000), and the hours equal the pristine |offset|/3600000. Rejected locations: Fraction.toProperString/getProperNumerator (negative proper strings already tested, and getProperNumerator would be a correct sibling); ArrayUtils.indexOf(double[],double,int,double tolerance) as an |a-v| <= tol chain (the existing tolerance tests catch a missing abs in both directions); CharUtils.unicodeEscaped nibble masks (0x999/0x1001 tests cover every nibble); StrBuilder clamps (class already used as a host; clamps tested); FastDateParser hour strategies (a pre-existing latent 'k' defect); BitField/Conversion/DurationFormatUtils (used). Scratch directories were deleted.
concerns: 1) Workarounds at decoys exist that were not declared because they absorb the fault. (a) H1 calls offsetMinuteField(Math.abs(offsetMillis)). G's contract accepts either sign, so an auditor may call this a small repair at a non-gold method, although G would still violate its own postcondition. (b) H3 writes Math.abs(minutes). (c) A one-line sink edit, (char) (Math.abs(value / 10) + '0'), absorbs because the trigger's minute field (30) ends in 0. (b) and (c) contradict 'passed on as given' / 'placed as given'. Choosing -03:45 would have blocked (c) but is not a real zone. 2) Secondary lure toward H1: H1 negates the truncated hours itself but hands G the signed offset. A model may argue that H1 should negate the offset (or the minutes) too. The documentation assigns sign handling of the minute field to G. 3) Recipe shape: E is several unchanged frames away from H1: format(long..) -> format(Date..) -> FastDateFormat/FastDatePrinter.format -> applyRules -> TimeZoneNumberRule.appendTo (context-edited to delegate). TimeZoneNumberRule.appendTo is not declared as a decoy, because FastDatePrinter has many identical appendTo(StringBuffer, Calendar) signatures that the G6 marker cannot tell apart. G is a leaf called by H1, so the order is a data flow G -> H1 -> H3 -> S, not a strict call chain H1 -> G -> H3 -> S. 4) The omission may be locally visible. G's single line divides the signed offset, while H1 visibly negates the hours, and the output '-03:-0' shows a sign leaking into the minutes. Strong models may hit a ceiling. 5) Host choices: G sits in DateUtils (a date-arithmetic class) rather than a formatting class. H3 shares DateFormatUtils with E. CharUtils hosted an earlier instance's helper (CharUtils::pair in USED_METHODS); appendTwoDigits is a new method. 6) Environment: on a JVM whose default time zone is negative and not a whole hour (e.g. America/St_Johns), default-zone formatting tests would also fail on the variant. Defects4J here runs under AEDT (positive), and the validator's G5 saw only the trigger fail.
revision: Revision 1 (2026-10-10, before any run). The independent audit rejected the first build on leakage only (item d). The gold's javadoc example ('+05:30 and -05:30 both give 30, -03:00 gives 0') repeated the trigger's zone literal 05:30, so a grep for it led to the gold. The example now reads '+09:45 and -09:45 both give 45, and -07:00 gives 0'. The contract sentence itself (minute field 0 to 59 whatever the sign) is unchanged, and no code changed. Every added production line (context edits and gold edit) was scanned for trigger literals (05:30, 03:30, 0530, 0330, 330, 210, 1000000000000, 12600000, 19800000, GMT, Locale.US, ZZ, 30, 03, 05); none remain. The other helpers' javadocs hold only 0..99, 0..59 and the sink examples 7 -> "07" and 42 -> "42", none of which occur in the trigger. Validator attempt 2 on this design: overall READY with every gate passing. Re-packaged; the variant id is still CTV-49DDB6.
